A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe EF-3DGS, and all 14 pages of v1.pdf and 11 pages of v3.pdf are readable. Neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement. Both reference supplementary material, and v3 specifically defers detailed results and analyses there, limiting verification of possible relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction and pose-estimation experiments on Tanks and Temples and RealEv-DAVIS, together with component ablations, pose-perturbation tests, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark results and component ablations in Tables 1–4 and reports pose-perturbation results in Figure 6, including comparisons with Event-3DGS.

M1.justification: The core framework remains, but several procedures change explicitly. Event warping changes from a symmetric temporal window to preceding frames, PBA selects the nearest previous RGB frame instead of adjacent frames, and the second Fixed-GS stage changes its stated objective from L_event to L_color (v1 Sections IV.B–D; v3 Sections 4.2–4.4).

E1.justification: Both versions use nine Tanks and Temples scenes and four RealEv-DAVIS scenes for novel-view synthesis and pose estimation. The five simulated frame rates, real-world SLOW/FAST scenarios, and pose-initialization perturbation scenario remain.

E2.justification: Event-3DGS (E+F) is added to the Tanks and Temples comparison and replaces ENeRF in the reported RealEv-DAVIS and pose-perturbation comparisons. Ev-Baseline is renamed EvCF-3DGS; its Time Lens plus CF-3DGS construction remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported Tanks and Temples preprocessing changes from downsampling to 1080p in v1 Section V.A to 4× spatial downsampling in v3 Section 5.1. The PDFs do not establish equivalent final resolutions or that experiments were rerun. Test-frame selection, temporal sampling, metrics, and test-pose optimization otherwise remain.

E4.justification: The component ablation is retained unchanged, while the pose-perturbation study replaces ENeRF with Event-3DGS. v1 additionally supplies subinterval/training-cost analysis, three loss-weight sweeps, and qualitative component studies. v3 refers hyperparameter studies and ablation visualizations to unavailable supplementary material, preventing a reliable judgment about their retention, revision, or removal.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The variance used in contrast maximization is an optimization objective, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All shared Tanks and Temples table values and all numerical component-ablation entries match. v3 adds Event-3DGS results, including 22.41 PSNR versus EF-3DGS's retained 23.96 at 1 FPS. Most RealEv-DAVIS aggregates reproduce v1's scene averages, but EF-3DGS SLOW SSIM is 0.6466 versus an average of 0.6666 from v1; missing detailed v3 results leave this discrepancy unresolved.

T1.justification: The IPWE definition changes from averaging a symmetric 2r+1-frame window to an r+1-frame preceding window. v3 also explicitly introduces locally linear motion to estimate the next pose for its gradient constraint (Section 4.2). These are limited mathematical and assumption changes; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The novelty claim, principal components, and joint reconstruction/pose-estimation contribution remain. The abstract raises the claimed PSNR advantage from up to 2 dB to up to 3 dB while retaining the 40% ATE claim. The larger PSNR difference was already present in v1's results, so this changes the headline claim rather than demonstrating improvement over v1.

C2.justification: The supplied v3 omits v1's explicit limitations concerning unordered images, motion blur, and scene-dependent manual parameter tuning. Detailed interpretations of computation and loss-weight tradeoffs are also no longer available in its text. Conversely, v3's introduction adds a substantive explanation that directly integrating differential event operations can amplify noise and produce ill-conditioned optimization.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies contrast thresholds of 0.25 and 0.21 and identifies COLMAP as the RealEv-DAVIS pose reference. The supplied text drops v1's explicit Adam parameters, PyTorch disclosure, CF-3DGS subsequence adaptation, hardware/timing information, and project-page link. Further implementation details are deferred to unavailable supplementary material.

R1.justification: v3 removes the dedicated large-scale reconstruction discussion, including its positioning against Mega-NeRF, Block-NeRF, CityGaussian, and VastGaussian. It refocuses the introduction on SLAM-inspired joint optimization and expands event-based positioning to discuss Event-3DGS and EaDeblur-GS. This substantially changes the literature framing despite retaining the central novelty claim.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations, and experimental discussion undergo extensive compression and rewriting. The large-scale related-work subsection and limitations section disappear from the supplied text, and lengthy component-specific discussions become a compact ablation narrative. This is substantial restructuring beyond renumbering or terminology changes.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the method overview and warping diagram, moves the teaser before the abstract, and merges and reduces dataset-specific rendering and trajectory panels. RealEv-DAVIS Tables III–IV become aggregate Table 3. The retained perturbation plots also change comparator labels and vertical-axis ranges, alongside extensive page-layout changes.

improvement.justification: v3 improves comparison relevance through Event-3DGS, clarifies the training overview, and supplies useful threshold values. However, explicit limitations disappear, substantial supporting analyses become inaccessible through references to missing supplementary material, and the RealEv-DAVIS SSIM discrepancy remains unexplained. These benefits and losses do not support a reliable net quality judgment from the supplied PDFs.
